Let’s talk about something every leader faces—emotional challenges. Welcome to Chapter 9: Leading with Emotional Agility.
Whether you’re leading a team officially, or just stepping up in the moment, you know it can feel like you’re expected to be calm, decisive, and upbeat—even when everything’s up in the air. But here’s the thing—pushing your feelings aside or pretending they’re not there? That can actually hurt your effectiveness, and even chip away at the trust you’ve built with your team.
Emotionally agile leaders see their own emotions—and the emotions of their team—not as obstacles, but as valuable signals. By showing openness, curiosity, and flexibility, they set the tone for a culture where people really feel seen, heard, and valued.
So, what does it actually look like to lead with emotional agility? Here are a few key practices to keep in mind:
First, acknowledge your own emotions. When you share what you’re feeling—appropriately, of course—you’re showing real vulnerability and authenticity. Next, encourage emotional expression on your team. Make it safe for folks to bring up concerns, share new ideas, and give honest feedback, without worrying they’ll be judged.
And finally, align your decisions with your shared values. When tough choices come up, let your organization’s values guide you—and be clear about how and why you’re making those moves.
Imagine a moment when your team’s facing a big change, like a company restructuring. An emotionally agile leader might say, “Hey, I know there’s a lot of anxiety and uncertainty right now.” Then, they’d share a vision that’s rooted in what matters most to the group. That kind of honesty doesn’t just ease nerves—it builds real trust and keeps everyone engaged, even when things get tough.
There’s another piece to this, too. Leaders who are emotionally agile don’t forget about self-care and boundaries. By taking care of themselves, they’re actually better at supporting others and staying effective over the long haul.
So, if you take one thing from this chapter, let it be this: Leading with emotional agility means balancing strength with vulnerability, clarity with compassion, and being decisive while staying open.
That’s how you build resilient, high-performing teams—and organizations that can weather any storm.
